chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Formaldehyde (HCHO) is treated with Water (H2O)?
questions.explanation: Treating Formaldehyde (HCHO) with Water (H2O) yields Methanediol (formalin, >99% gem-diol). Rationale: Formaldehyde lacks steric hindrance and electron donation, favoring complete hydration to gem-diol.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzaldehyde (PhCHO) into Mandelonitrile (2-hydroxy-2-phenylacetonitrile)?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzaldehyde (PhCHO) into Mandelonitrile (2-hydroxy-2-phenylacetonitrile), the appropriate reagent is Sodium cyanide (NaCN) / HCl. Rationale: Nucleophilic addition of cyanide to the carbonyl carbon followed by protonation yields the cyanohydrin.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Cyclohexanone is treated with Aniline (PhNH2) / trace acid catalyst?
questions.explanation: Treating Cyclohexanone with Aniline (PhNH2) / trace acid catalyst yields N-Cyclohexylidenebenzenamine + H2O. Rationale: Primary amine adds to carbonyl; elimination of water through carbinolamine intermediate yields the imine.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Cyclohexanone into 1-(Cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)pyrrolidine + H2O?
questions.explanation: To convert Cyclohexanone into 1-(Cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)pyrrolidine + H2O, the appropriate reagent is Pyrrolidine / trace acid catalyst (Dean-Stark). Rationale: Secondary amine adds to carbonyl; loss of water requires proton abstraction from alpha-carbon forming enamine.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Cyclohexanone is treated with Ethylene glycol (HOCH2CH2OH) / p-TsOH?
questions.explanation: Treating Cyclohexanone with Ethylene glycol (HOCH2CH2OH) / p-TsOH yields 1,4-Dioxaspiro[4.5]decane (cyclic ethylene acetal) + H2O. Rationale: Acid-catalyzed addition of diol with water removal protects the carbonyl against nucleophiles and bases.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1,4-Dioxaspiro[4.5]decane into Cyclohexanone + Ethylene glycol?
questions.explanation: To convert 1,4-Dioxaspiro[4.5]decane into Cyclohexanone + Ethylene glycol, the appropriate reagent is Aqueous 1 M HCl / heat. Rationale: Hydrolysis in aqueous acid Le Chatelier equilibrium regenerates the parent ketone and diol.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Hydrazine (N2H4), KOH / diethylene glycol (200°C) to yield Ethylbenzene (PhCH2CH3) + N2 gas as the major product?
questions.explanation: Acetophenone (PhCOCH3) reacts with Hydrazine (N2H4), KOH / diethylene glycol (200°C) to yield Ethylbenzene (PhCH2CH3) + N2 gas. Rationale: Hydrazone intermediate undergoes base-catalyzed proton transfers and loss of nitrogen gas to yield alkane.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Cyclohexanone is treated with Methylenetriphenylphosphorane (Ph3P=CH2)?
questions.explanation: Treating Cyclohexanone with Methylenetriphenylphosphorane (Ph3P=CH2) yields Methylenecyclohexane + Triphenylphosphine oxide (Ph3P=O). Rationale: Phosphonium ylide reacts via a 4-membered oxaphosphetane ring, replacing C=O with C=CH2.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Triethyl phosphonoacetate + NaH to yield (E)-Ethyl cinnamate (trans-alkene ester) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde reacts with Triethyl phosphonoacetate + NaH to yield (E)-Ethyl cinnamate (trans-alkene ester). Rationale: Phosphonate ester carbanion adds to aldehyde, eliminating diethyl phosphate to form trans-alpha,beta-unsaturated ester.

questions.chapter_title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Cyclohexen-1-one is treated with 1. Lithium dimethylcuprate ((CH3)2CuLi); 2. H3O+?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Cyclohexen-1-one with 1. Lithium dimethylcuprate ((CH3)2CuLi); 2. H3O+ yields 3-Methylcyclohexanone. Rationale: Soft organocuprate nucleophile adds selectively to the beta-carbon of the alpha,beta-unsaturated enone.
